domain: Gamelan set-making and ensemble tuning — the Javanese and Balinese craft in which instruments are forged, tuned and named as one indivisible set (a seprangkat, commonly a named pair of sléndro and pélog): the embat, each set's own interval flavour deliberately left unstandardized so that no reference pitch exists outside the set; ngumbang-ngisep, the Balinese paired tuning that holds two near-identical instruments slightly apart to produce the ombak, the acoustic beating that is the set's actual voice; the rule that an instrument borrowed from another gamelan is unusable in this one however fine it is alone; the balungan that underdetermines every player's part, leaving garap and cengkok to conventions the players hold between them rather than in any score; and the smith who forges a replacement key blank and tunes it by ear in the room, against the instruments it will stand beside, never against a standard
axioms: The set is the unit, not the instrument; an instrument has no properties worth naming apart from the neighbours it was tuned against.
Set-membership is invisible on the object and audible only when the members sound together — so it is exactly the property a per-item store forgets first.
There is no standard pitch. Two sets that both sound correct are correct by differing, and tuning either to an external reference spoils it.
A borrowed instrument fails not because it is worse but because it was tuned against different neighbours; excellence does not transfer between sets.
A replacement is tuned in the room it is entering, by ear, against what it will stand beside — never in the workshop and never to a specification.
Two near-identical members held slightly apart are not a duplicate; the difference between them is the sound the set was built to make.
Painted labels are not identity: instruments bearing the same name in two gamelans are two instruments, and joining them by the label produces a set nobody can play.
Which parts cover which register is held between the players as convention, not written down — so the moment a member is swapped, the coverage is only assumed.
primitives: the set (the panel — the lenses one review generates and dispatches together: spec files of 3, 2, 1, 1, 1 in this run, coordinated through each lens's `anti_overlap` naming its siblings by id)
embat (the deliberate mutual spacing a review's lenses were given — what melange's seed and STEER-WIDE staging exists to produce)

the borrowed instrument (Task 16's `materialize`, writing the stored body verbatim into `<agents_dir>/<spec name>.md`, overriding only `tier`/`registry_id`/`reused_at`/`source_spec` and keeping `name`/`description`)
the imported neighbours (the reused body's rendered `## Task Context` and `anti_overlap_section` — generate-agents.py — naming another review's target and another review's siblings)
the deaf ear (`thresholds.embedding_text` = persona + focus + decision_lens + review_areas, structurally excluding `anti_overlap` and `task_context`)

tuning in the room (what fresh generation does and reuse does not: Task 17 resolves before the `name in existing` check and `continue`s, so the new spec's own `anti_overlap` and `task_context` are never rendered)

joining by the painted label (Task 12's `variant-of` union-find joining on cosine `≥ VARIANT_MIN_COSINE` **or identical `name`**; measured pile: 3,023 files, 1,776 names, 1,799 bodies, 21 names holding 44 distinct bodies)
the one servable instrument (`load()` returning heads only; `resolveLens` skipping non-heads)
admission on the label alone (the lexical fallback's exact-`name` rule, reached when local Ollama and the Tailscale fallback both miss the 4 s timeout)
the ombak (deliberate near-pairs — a fusion beside its parents, a retargeted variant beside its base — collapsed by clustering at `≥ 0.92`)

the dissolved set (sighting rows and frontmatter carrying no run/panel/cohort field; `merge.py` decomposing the spec file under 'first sighting with a spec wins'; Task 23 deleting `.claude/flux-gen-specs/`)
the mixed set nobody listens to (Task 17's per-spec loop assembling a panel from several sets, each member individually above `RESOLVE_MIN_COSINE`, with no step reading the group)
failure_mode: Cannot check a number — thresholds, cosines, dimensions and hit-rate math pass unexamined, and the trade's own doctrine is that no standard exists to check them against.
Indifferent to schema and semantics: edge predicates, cardinality, direction, head election and traversal can all be wrong and this lens will not look.
Sees two machines as two sets that are correct by differing, so races, merge conflicts, partitions and ordinary split-brain are invisible to it.
Has no view on whether any individual lens is good, well written, well named, or correctly rendered — quality of the member is entirely outside its frame.
Blind to time: decay, staleness, cadence, obligation and who runs a recurring pass never register, because a set left alone for a decade is still in tune with itself.
Structurally hostile to transfer, so it will resist reuse that is simply fine, and can demand that set-membership be recorded where the recording costs more than the mismatch.
Prone to unfalsifiable ensemble claims — 'the panel does not cohere' is easy to assert and hard to act on unless forced to name the two sets and the differing neighbour.
Will not notice a wrong, truncated or battered record, nor how entries are filed or retrieved; a sound instrument from the wrong set is its only category of fault.
